prompt: State two characteristics of a system in dynamic equilibrium.
markscheme: Any two **(A2)**: forward and backward rates are equal; concentrations remain constant (not necessarily equal); it requires a closed system; macroscopic properties are constant while reactions continue.

prompt: Write the equilibrium constant expression for $\text{N}_2(g)+3\text{H}_2(g)\rightleftharpoons2\text{NH}_3(g)$.
For an exothermic reaction, K is very large at 300 K. Which statement is correct?
options: The equilibrium mixture contains mainly products.
markscheme: **C.** A large K means the mixture is mostly products at equilibrium. For an exothermic reaction, raising the temperature decreases K. A catalyst does not change K.

prompt: For $\text{N}_2(g)+3\text{H}_2(g)\rightleftharpoons2\text{NH}_3(g)$, ΔH = −92 kJ, predict and explain the effect on the yield of ammonia of **(a)** increasing the pressure and **(b)** increasing the temperature.
markscheme:
**(a)** Increases: the equilibrium shifts to the side with fewer moles of gas (2 vs 4), reducing the pressure **(A1)(R1)**

**(b)** Decreases: the forward reaction is exothermic, so the equilibrium shifts in the endothermic (backward) direction to absorb the heat **(A1)**

prompt: For a reaction with $K_c=50$ at a certain temperature, a mixture has $Q=12$. Predict the direction in which the reaction proceeds.
markscheme: $Q<K$, so the ratio of products to reactants is too small **(R1)**; the forward reaction is favoured until $Q=K$ **(A1)**

prompt: 1.00 mol of H₂ and 1.00 mol of I₂ are placed in a 1.00 dm³ flask. $\text{H}_2+\text{I}_2\rightleftharpoons2\text{HI}$, $K_c=50.0$. Calculate the equilibrium concentration of HI.
A reaction has $K=1.0\times10^{-5}$ at 298 K. Calculate ΔG° and comment on the position of equilibrium. ($R=8.31\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$)
markscheme: $\Delta G^{\circ}=-RT\ln K=-8.31\times298\times\ln(1.0\times10^{-5})=+28.5\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ **(A1)**; positive ΔG° and small K: reactants predominate at equilibrium **(R1)**
